title: Murder (Malice Murder)
description: A person commits the offense of murder when he unlawfully and with malice aforethought, either express or implied, causes the death of another human being. Malice murder is among Georgia's 'Seven Deadly Sins' - the most serious violent felonies.

options.label: Life Imprisonment (with parole eligibility)
options.other: Parole eligibility after 30 years for offenses committed on or after July 1, 2006.

options.label: Death Penalty (if sought by State)
options.other: Requires statutory aggravating circumstances under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-30.

notes: First Offender treatment is PROHIBITED under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.1.
recidivist_info: A person convicted of a second serious violent felony shall be sentenced to Life Without Parole under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-7(b)(2).
parole_info: As a '7 Deadly Sin' offense, murder is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences (parole eligibility after 30 years). Conspiracy or attempt to commit murder is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: Felony Murder
description: A person commits felony murder when, in the commission of a felony, he or she causes the death of another human being irrespective of malice. The underlying felony merges with the murder conviction.
notes: The underlying felony merges with the felony murder conviction. Intent to kill is NOT required - only intent to commit the underlying felony.
recidivist_info: Second serious violent felony conviction mandates Life Without Parole.
parole_info: As a '7 Deadly Sin' offense, felony murder is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences (parole eligibility after 30 years). Conspiracy or attempt to commit felony murder is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: Murder in the Second Degree
description: A person commits murder in the second degree when, in the commission of cruelty to children in the second degree, he or she causes the death of another human being irrespective of malice.
notes: Unlike malice murder or felony murder, second degree murder is NOT a 'Serious Violent Felony' and does not carry the 30-year parole restriction.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 6. Not a '7 Deadly Sin' offense. Parole eligibility requires serving 65% of the sentence for non-violent classification or 90% if designated BDV (Board-Designated Violent) based on case circumstances.

title: Trafficking in Fentanyl
description: Possession, sale, or delivery of 4 grams or more of fentanyl or a mixture containing fentanyl. Mandatory minimums apply.
notes: Sentencing under 2024 FEAR Act. Extremely strict liability.
recidivist_info: Mandatory Minimums apply. DEVIATIONS: (1) Substantial Assistance (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(g)(2)) - Judge may reduce sentence if defendant provides substantial help to police. (2) Judicial Safety Valve - Judge may depart from mandatory min if: No weapon, no death/injury, no prior felony drug conviction, not a leader, and interests of justice served.
parole_info: For tier 3 (Level 3) trafficking reduced to Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) via plea, the Crime Severity Level (CSL) is often determined by the original drug weight found in the lab report unless the weight itself is also explicitly reduced in the plea agreement.

title: Possession of Schedule I or II Controlled Substance
description: Unlawful possession of Schedule I (e.g., Heroin, LSD, MDMA) or Sched II Narcotic (e.g., Cocaine, Meth, Oxycodone).
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and weight. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Schedule I/II possession is not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Schedule III, IV, or V
description: Unlawful possession of Schedule III (Steroids, Ketamine), IV (Xanax, Valium), or V (Codeine cough syrup).
notes: Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol) has enhanced penalties (5-30 years).
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 1-2 depending on offense history. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Trafficking in Cocaine
description: Possession, sale, or delivery of 28 grams or more of cocaine/mixture.
recidivist_info: Mandatory Minimums apply. DEVIATIONS: (1) Substantial Assistance (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(g)(2)) - Judge may reduce sentence for help. (2) Judicial Safety Valve - Departure allowed if: No weapon, no death/injury, no prior felony drug conviction, not a leader.
parole_info: For tier 3 (Level 3) trafficking reduced to Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) via plea, the Crime Severity Level (CSL) is often determined by the original drug weight found in the lab report unless the weight itself is also explicitly reduced in the plea agreement.

title: Trafficking in Methamphetamine
description: Possession, sale, or delivery of 28 grams or more of methamphetamine/mixture.
recidivist_info: Mandatory Minimums apply. DEVIATIONS: (1) Substantial Assistance (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(g)(2)) - Judge may reduce sentence for help. (2) Judicial Safety Valve - Departure allowed if: No weapon, no death/injury, no prior felony drug conviction, not a leader.
parole_info: For tier 3 (Level 3) trafficking reduced to Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) via plea, the Crime Severity Level (CSL) is often determined by the original drug weight found in the lab report unless the weight itself is also explicitly reduced in the plea agreement.

title: Trafficking in Heroin/Opioids
description: Possession, sale, or delivery of 4 grams or more of heroin, morphine, or opium.
recidivist_info: Mandatory Minimums apply. DEVIATIONS: (1) Substantial Assistance (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(g)(2)) - Judge may reduce sentence for help. (2) Judicial Safety Valve - Departure allowed if: No weapon, no death/injury, no prior felony drug conviction, not a leader.
parole_info: For tier 3 (Level 3) trafficking reduced to Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) via plea, the Crime Severity Level (CSL) is often determined by the original drug weight found in the lab report unless the weight itself is also explicitly reduced in the plea agreement.

title: Trafficking in Marijuana
description: Possession, sale, or delivery of more than 10 lbs of marijuana. All trafficking carries maximum 30 years imprisonment.
recidivist_info: Mandatory Minimums apply. DEVIATIONS: (1) Substantial Assistance (O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(g)(2)) - Judge may reduce sentence for help. (2) Judicial Safety Valve - Departure allowed if: No weapon, no death/injury, no prior felony drug conviction, not a leader.
parole_info: For tier 3 (Level 3) trafficking reduced to Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) via plea, the Crime Severity Level (CSL) is often determined by the original drug weight found in the lab report unless the weight itself is also explicitly reduced in the plea agreement.

title: Trafficking in MDMA/MDA (Ecstasy/Molly)
description: A person who sells, delivers, brings into this state, or has possession of 28 grams or more of 3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA) or 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), or any mixture containing either substance, commits the felony offense of trafficking in ecstasy. Mandatory minimum sentences and fines increase with weight.

title: Possession of Marijuana (Less than 1 oz)
description: Possession of 1 ounce or less of marijuana.
notes: Often eligible for pre-trial diversion or city ordinance violations in some jurisdictions.
parole_info: Misdemeanor offense - parole does not apply. Sentence served as jail time (up to 12 months). May be eligible for early release programs or time served credits.

title: Possession of Marijuana (More than 1 oz)
description: Possession of more than 1 ounce of marijuana.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Terroristic Threats
description: Threatening to commit a crime of violence, release hazardous substance, or burn property.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for general threats (misdemeanor), CSL 5 for death threats or threats against judges/police (felony). Felony terroristic threats require serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility unless designated BDV.

title: Criminal Street Gang Activity
description: Participation in criminal gang activity or commission of an offense to further gang interests.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) for gang charges is 5 for offenses committed prior to July 1, 2023, and CSL 8 for offenses committed on or after July 1, 2023.

title: Aggravated Assault
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Aggravated Assault is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Statutory Rape
description: Sexual intercourse with a person under 16 years of age who is not the defendant's spouse. Romeo & Juliet exception applies if victim is 14-15 and defendant is 18 or younger and within 4 years of victim's age.

options.label: Victim under 16; Defendant under 21
options.other: Sex offender registration required

options.label: Victim under 16; Defendant 21 or older
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 10 years before parole eligibility

options.label: Romeo & Juliet Exception (Victim 14-15; Defendant ≤18 and within 4 years)
options.other: Sex offender registration required (misdemeanor classification)

notes: Consent is not a defense to statutory rape if victim is under 16. Age of consent in Georgia is 16. First offender treatment is NOT available for statutory rape convictions.
recidivist_info: All statutory rape convictions require sex offender registration under O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12. Defendants 21+ receive mandatory minimums under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.2, including at least one year of probation after release. No possibility of sentence reduction or expungement.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 5 for defendant under 21, CSL 8 for defendant 21 or older. Statutory rape with defendant 21+ is a BDV offense requiring 90% of sentence before parole eligibility. Romeo & Juliet misdemeanor: parole does not apply.

title: Child Molestation
description: Performing immoral or indecent acts to or in the presence of a child under 16 with the intent to arouse or satisfy sexual desires. Includes electronic transmission of indecent material to a child.

options.label: Child Molestation - 1st Offense
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 5 years before parole eligibility

options.label: Child Molestation - 2nd or Subsequent Offense
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 10 years before parole eligibility; enhanced supervision

options.label: Aggravated Child Molestation (physical injury or sodomy)
options.sentence: 25 years to Life (Mandatory min 25 years without parole)
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 25 years with no parole, probation, or suspension; split sentence possible after 25 years (probation for life)

options.label: Romeo & Juliet Exception (Victim 13-15; Defendant ≤18 and within 4 years; sodomy only)
options.other: Sex offender registration required

notes: First offender treatment is SPECIFICALLY PROHIBITED under Georgia law for child molestation convictions. Electronic monitoring may be required as condition of probation. Aggravated child molestation requires actual physical injury or sodomy.
recidivist_info: Mandatory registration as sex offender within 72 hours of release under O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12. Aggravated child molestation carries mandatory 25 years without possibility of parole, probation, or sentence suspension for first 25 years. No reduction possible except in extraordinary cases under appellate review.
parole_info: AGGRAVATED Child Molestation is a '7 Deadly Sin' offense and is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences. Conspiracy or attempt to commit aggravated child molestation is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: Aggravated Sexual Battery
description: Intentionally penetrating the sexual organ or anus of another person with a foreign object (any article or instrument other than the sexual organ) without consent. One of Georgia's most severely punished sex crimes.

options.label: No Prior Sexual Felony
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 25 years - cannot be reduced by court or parole; split sentence possible after 25 years (probation for life)

options.label: Prior Sexual Felony Conviction
options.sentence: Life or Life with Probation (Mandatory min 25 years)
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required; Must serve 25 years minimum; mandatory electronic monitoring as condition of probation

notes: Amendments effective May 4, 2023, apply to offenses committed on or after July 1, 2023. 'Foreign object' means any article or instrument other than the sexual organ. Mandatory minimum of 25 years must be served before parole eligibility.
recidivist_info: Subject to sentencing provisions under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.1 and § 17-10-7. Split sentences allow 25+ years imprisonment followed by lifetime probation. Electronic monitoring required for all probationary periods for repeat offenders. No first offender treatment available. Lifetime sex offender registration under O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12.
parole_info: As a '7 Deadly Sin' offense, aggravated sexual battery is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences. Conspiracy or attempt to commit aggravated sexual battery is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: DUI - Driving Under the Influence
description: Driving while under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or toxic vapors. Criminal lookback is 10 years; license suspension lookback is 5 years.

options.label: 1st Offense
options.other: License suspension: 12 months (limited permit after 120 days); Time served during arrest may count toward 24-hour minimum

options.label: 2nd Offense
options.other: License suspension: 18 months if within 5 years of prior DUI; 12 months otherwise; All except 72 hours may be suspended

options.label: 3rd Offense
options.other: License revocation: 5 years; Habitual Violator status; All except 15 days may be suspended

options.label: 4th Offense (Felony)
options.other: License revocation: 5 years; Must serve 1-year minimum; Cannot be suspended, probated, or reduced; Habitual Violator status

notes: Criminal penalties use 10-year lookback (date of arrest to date of arrest). License consequences use 5-year lookback for enhanced suspensions. Only convictions on or after July 1, 2008 count toward felony enhancement.
recidivist_info: Fourth DUI within 10 years triggers felony prosecution under O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391(c)(4). All DUI convictions remain on record for life. No first offender treatment available after conviction.
parole_info: 1st-3rd offense DUI (misdemeanor): Parole does not apply; sentence served as jail time. 4th offense DUI (felony): Crime Severity Level (CSL) 1. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Armed Robbery
notes: Mandatory 10-year minimum must be served in full with no possibility of parole. No portion can be suspended, stayed, probated, deferred, or withheld unless the State agrees to sentence below minimum.
parole_info: As a '7 Deadly Sin' offense, armed robbery is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences. Conspiracy or attempt to commit armed robbery is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: Theft by Taking
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies by value: CSL 1 (misdemeanor, under $1,500), CSL 2 ($1,500-$5,000), CSL 3 ($5,000-$25,000), CSL 4 ($25,000+). Felony theft requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Burglary in the First Degree
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Burglary in the First Degree (residential burglary) is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Burglary in the Second Degree
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Burglary in the Second Degree (non-residential) requires serving 65% of the sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Psilocybin (Mushrooms)
description: Possession of any amount of Psilocybin (Schedule I). No specific 'Trafficking' weight tier exists; high volume is prosecuted as Possession with Intent.
notes: Possession with Intent to Distribute carries 5-30 years (1st Offense) or 10-40 years (2nd Offense).
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on amount and offense history. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Financial Transaction Card Theft
description: Taking, obtaining, or withholding a credit/debit card without consent.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Financial Transaction Card Fraud
description: Using a card that is forged, expired, revoked, or belongs to another.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for amounts not exceeding $100 (misdemeanor), CSL 2 for amounts exceeding $100 (felony). Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Forgery in the First Degree
description: Knowingly making, altering, or possessing a writing (other than a check) in a fictitious name or in such manner that it purports to have been made by another person, and uttering or delivering such writing with intent to defraud.
notes: Uttering or delivery is an essential element distinguishing 1st from 2nd degree.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Forgery in the Second Degree
description: Knowingly making, altering, or possessing a writing (other than a check) in a fictitious name or in such manner that it purports to have been made by another person, with intent to defraud. Differs from 1st degree in that uttering/delivery is NOT required.
notes: Possession alone with intent to defraud is sufficient; no need to present or deliver the writing.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Forgery in the Third Degree
description: Knowingly making, altering, possessing, or delivering any check for $1,500 or more OR 10 or more checks (regardless of amount) in a fictitious name or manner indicating it was made by another person, with intent to defraud.
notes: Check-specific forgery for amounts over $1,500 or volume of 10+ checks.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Forgery in the Fourth Degree
description: Knowingly making, altering, possessing, or delivering checks that do not meet 3rd degree thresholds (under $1,500 or fewer than 10 checks), with intent to defraud. Classification depends on offense history.
notes: First two convictions are misdemeanors; third and subsequent convictions elevate to felony status.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for 1st and 2nd offense (misdemeanor), CSL 2 for 3rd or subsequent offense (felony). Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
description: Willfully failing or refusing to bring a vehicle to a stop or attempting to flee from a pursuing police officer after being given a visual or audible signal to stop. Officer must be in uniform with badge displayed and vehicle must be marked as official police vehicle.

options.label: Fleeing with 20+ mph over speed limit
options.other: Must serve 1-year minimum - cannot be suspended, probated, deferred, withheld, reduced, or merged with other offenses

options.label: Fleeing with collision (vehicle or pedestrian)
options.other: Must serve 1-year minimum - cannot be suspended, probated, deferred, withheld, reduced, or merged with other offenses

options.label: Fleeing in traffic conditions creating public risk
options.other: Must serve 1-year minimum - cannot be suspended, probated, deferred, withheld, reduced, or merged with other offenses

options.label: 4th or Subsequent Offense (within 10 years)
options.other: Must serve 1-year minimum - cannot be suspended, probated, deferred, withheld, reduced, or merged with other offenses

notes: First three offenses are high and aggravated misdemeanors unless elevated to felony by dangerous circumstances. Officer must be in uniform with badge and in marked vehicle. Signal to stop must be visual or audible.
recidivist_info: Fourth conviction within 10 years is automatic felony. Felony convictions carry mandatory sentences that cannot be suspended, probated, deferred, withheld, reduced to lesser offense, merged with other offenses, or served concurrently.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3 for felony fleeing/eluding. Misdemeanor offenses: parole does not apply. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Obstruction of a Law Enforcement Officer
description: Knowingly and willfully obstructing, hindering, or resisting a law enforcement officer in the lawful discharge of their official duties. Felony if violence is used against officer or bodily fluids are thrown at officer.

options.label: Basic Obstruction (without violence)
options.other: Mandatory minimum $300 fine in addition to any other penalties

options.label: Obstruction with Violence to Officer
options.other: Mandatory minimum $300 fine; violence includes offering or doing violence to person of officer

options.label: Throwing Bodily Fluids at Officer
options.other: Mandatory minimum $300 fine; bodily fluids include blood, urine, feces, vomitus, or seminal fluid

notes: All convictions require mandatory minimum $300 fine in addition to other penalties. Officer must be acting in lawful discharge of official duties. Felony applies when violence is offered/done to officer OR when bodily fluids are thrown/projected at officer.
recidivist_info: No specific recidivist enhancement provisions, but prior convictions may be considered at sentencing. Violence requirement for felony means any physical force or threat of force against the officer's person.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for basic obstruction (misdemeanor), CSL 3 for felony obstruction with violence. Misdemeanor: parole does not apply. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
description: Failure to comply with sex offender registration requirements, including failing to register initially within 72 hours, failing to report address changes within 72 hours, or failing to appear in person at the sheriff's office within 72 hours of birthday for annual verification.

options.label: First Offense
options.other: Strict liability offense - intent is not required. No judicial discretion below statutory minimum.

options.label: Second or Subsequent Offense
options.other: Mandatory 5-year minimum cannot be suspended, probated, or reduced.

notes: This is a STRICT LIABILITY offense - the State does not need to prove intent. Missing a deadline by even one day carries the same penalties as deliberate evasion. Common violations include: failing to register within 72 hours of release or moving to Georgia, failing to report address changes within 72 hours, missing annual birthday verification, and failing to report employment or school changes.
recidivist_info: Second offense triggers mandatory 5-year minimum with no judicial discretion. Violations of residency/employment restrictions under O.C.G.A. § 42-1-15 carry separate penalties of 10 to 30 years.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 5 for first offense, CSL 7 for second or subsequent offense. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense, but strict mandatory minimums apply.

title: Possession of Tools for Commission of Crime
description: A person commits this offense when they have in their possession any tool, explosive, or other device commonly used in the commission of burglary, theft, or other crime with the intent to make use thereof in the commission of a crime.
notes: Both possession AND intent to use the tools to commit a crime must be proven. Possessing tools that could be used in committing a crime is not in itself a crime - intent is required. The tool must be one commonly used for the commission of the specific crime alleged.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Theft by Receiving Stolen Property
description: A person commits this offense when they receive, dispose of, or retain stolen property which they know or should know was stolen, unless the property is received, disposed of, or retained with intent to restore it to the owner.
notes: 'Receiving' means acquiring possession or control or lending on the security of the property. In any prosecution, it is not necessary to show a conviction of the principal thief. Knowledge that property was stolen can be actual or constructive ('should have known').
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies by value: CSL 1 (misdemeanor, under $1,500), CSL 2 ($1,500-$5,000), CSL 3 ($5,000-$25,000), CSL 4 ($25,000+). Felony theft by receiving requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Stalking
description: A person commits stalking when they follow, place under surveillance, or contact another person at or about a place or places without consent for the purpose of harassing and intimidating that person.
notes: Before sentencing, the judge may require psychological evaluation of the offender and shall consider the entire criminal record. The judge may issue a permanent restraining order and may require psychological treatment as part of the sentence or as a condition of probation.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for first offense (misdemeanor), CSL 5 for second or subsequent offense (felony). Felony stalking is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of sentence before parole eligibility.

title: Aggravated Stalking
description: A person commits aggravated stalking when they violate a protective order, bond, injunction, or condition of pretrial release/probation/parole prohibiting such behavior, and follows, places under surveillance, or contacts another person without consent for the purpose of harassing and intimidating that person.
notes: Aggravated stalking requires violation of an existing court order (such as a temporary protective order, permanent protective order, preliminary injunction, bond to keep the peace, or conditions of probation/parole) in addition to the stalking conduct. The judge may require psychological evaluation and treatment, and may issue a permanent restraining order at sentencing.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Aggravated Stalking is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Possession of Cocaine
description: Unlawful possession of cocaine (Schedule II Narcotic) in any amount less than 28 grams. Possession of 28 grams or more triggers trafficking charges under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31 with mandatory minimum sentences.
notes: Trafficking threshold: 28 grams. Possession of 28g+ triggers mandatory minimums under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31. Conditional discharge under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-2(a) may be available for eligible first offenders (probation without adjudication of guilt). Drug Court under O.C.G.A. § 15-1-15 may also be available.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Methamphetamine
description: Unlawful possession of methamphetamine (Schedule II) in any amount less than 28 grams. Possession of 28 grams or more triggers trafficking charges under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(e) with mandatory minimum sentences.
notes: Trafficking threshold: 28 grams. Possession of 28g+ triggers mandatory minimums under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(e). Conditional discharge under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-2(a) may be available for eligible first offenders. Drug Court under O.C.G.A. § 15-1-15 may also be available.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Fentanyl
description: Unlawful possession of fentanyl (Schedule II Narcotic) in any amount less than 4 grams. Possession of 4 grams or more triggers trafficking charges under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31 (FEAR Act) with severe mandatory minimum sentences.
notes: Trafficking threshold: 4 grams (FEAR Act) - one of the lowest trafficking thresholds in Georgia. Possession of 4g+ triggers mandatory minimums starting at 10 years. Conditional discharge under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-2(a) may be available for eligible first offenders. Drug Court under O.C.G.A. § 15-1-15 may also be available.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Heroin
description: Unlawful possession of heroin (Schedule I) in any amount less than 4 grams. Possession of 4 grams or more triggers trafficking charges under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(b) with mandatory minimum sentences.
notes: Trafficking threshold: 4 grams. Possession of 4g+ triggers mandatory minimums under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31(b). Conditional discharge under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-2(a) may be available for eligible first offenders. Drug Court under O.C.G.A. § 15-1-15 may also be available.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of MDMA (Ecstasy/Molly)
description: Unlawful possession of MDMA/Ecstasy/Molly (Schedule I). Georgia does not have a specific trafficking weight threshold for MDMA; large quantities are prosecuted as Possession with Intent to Distribute.
notes: No specific trafficking weight threshold exists for MDMA in Georgia. Large quantities may be charged as Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-30(b) (5-30 years, 1st offense). Conditional discharge under O.C.G.A. § 16-13-2(a) may be available for eligible first offenders.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3-4 depending on offense history and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Theft by Shoplifting
description: A person commits theft by shoplifting when they, alone or in concert with others, take possession of or carry away merchandise, alter price tags, transfer merchandise between containers, interchange labels, or wrongfully cause the amount paid to be less than the merchant's stated price.
notes: Felony threshold for shoplifting is $500 (lower than the $1,500 general theft threshold under O.C.G.A. § 16-8-12). Third or subsequent shoplifting conviction within 10 years is a felony regardless of the value of merchandise. Organized retail crime involving three or more persons may carry enhanced penalties.
recidivist_info: Third or subsequent conviction within 10 years: Felony (1-10 years) regardless of value. Photo and fingerprints taken on second offense and forwarded to GBI. Repeated shoplifting convictions cannot be reduced below felony status on third or subsequent offense.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies: CSL 1 for misdemeanor, CSL 2-3 for felony depending on value and offense history. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Simple Assault
description: A person commits simple assault when they either attempt to commit a violent injury to another person or commit an act which places another in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving a violent injury.

options.label: Against public school employee on school property
In a public transit vehicle or station

notes: Simple assault is a lesser included offense of aggravated assault. No physical contact is required - placing someone in reasonable apprehension of injury is sufficient.
parole_info: Misdemeanor offense - parole does not apply. Sentence served as jail time (up to 12 months).

title: Simple Battery
description: A person commits simple battery when they either intentionally make physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature with the person of another, or intentionally cause physical harm to another.

options.label: Against police officer or first responder

notes: High and aggravated misdemeanor classification applies when the victim is 65+, pregnant, a police officer, corrections officer, or other specified persons. For family violence simple battery, see Family Violence Battery entry.
parole_info: Misdemeanor offense - parole does not apply. Sentence served as jail time.

title: Battery
description: A person commits battery when they intentionally cause substantial physical harm or visible bodily harm to another. Visible bodily harm means bodily harm capable of being perceived by a person other than the victim, including bruises, lacerations, swelling, or abrasions.

options.label: Against police officer or first responder

notes: 'Visible bodily harm' means bruises, lacerations, swelling, or abrasions perceptible to others. 'Substantial physical harm' means harm beyond what is visible. For family violence battery, see the Family Violence Battery entry.
parole_info: CSL 1 for misdemeanor battery, CSL 3 for felony battery. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Generally not a BDV offense.

title: Aggravated Battery
description: A person commits aggravated battery when they maliciously cause bodily harm to another by depriving them of a member of their body, by rendering a member of their body useless, or by seriously disfiguring their body or a member thereof.

options.label: Against police officer or corrections officer

notes: Aggravated battery against a police officer, corrections officer, or other specified public safety officer carries a mandatory minimum of 10 years. 'Maliciously' means with the deliberate intention to do wrong.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Aggravated Battery is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Family Violence Battery
description: Battery committed between past or present spouses, persons who are parents of the same child, parents and children, stepparents and stepchildren, foster parents and foster children, or other persons living or formerly living in the same household.
notes: Prior family violence convictions from ANY jurisdiction count toward recidivist enhancement. 'Family violence' includes battery, simple battery, simple assault, stalking, criminal damage to property, unlawful restraint, or criminal trespass between household members. A Temporary Protective Order (TPO) is commonly issued alongside charges.
recidivist_info: Second family violence conviction: mandatory minimum 10 days jail. Third or subsequent conviction: Felony (1-5 years). Prior convictions from other states count toward enhancement.
parole_info: CSL 1 for misdemeanor, CSL 3 for felony family violence battery. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. May be designated BDV depending on circumstances.

title: Voluntary Manslaughter
description: A person commits voluntary manslaughter when they cause the death of another human being under circumstances which would otherwise be murder and if they act solely as the result of a sudden, violent, and irresistible passion resulting from serious provocation sufficient to excite such passion in a reasonable person.
notes: Voluntary manslaughter is a lesser included offense of murder. The key element is 'sudden heat of passion' caused by 'serious provocation' - the defendant must have acted immediately upon the provocation without time to cool down. If there was time to cool down, the charge reverts to murder.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Voluntary Manslaughter is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Involuntary Manslaughter
description: A person commits involuntary manslaughter when they cause the death of another human being without any intention to do so.

options.label: During commission of unlawful act (not a felony)
During commission of lawful act in unlawful manner

notes: If death occurs during commission of a felony, the proper charge is typically felony murder under O.C.G.A. § 16-5-1(c), not involuntary manslaughter. Misdemeanor involuntary manslaughter is often seen in negligence-related deaths.
parole_info: CSL varies: CSL 1 for misdemeanor involuntary manslaughter, CSL 5 for felony involuntary manslaughter. Felony may be designated BDV requiring 90% service.

title: Vehicular Homicide
description: Causing the death of another person through the violation of traffic laws. First degree involves DUI-related deaths or deaths caused by habitual violator/fleeing and eluding. Second degree involves deaths caused by other traffic violations.
notes: 1st degree vehicular homicide requires proof that the defendant was DUI (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391), a habitual violator (O.C.G.A. § 40-5-58), or fleeing/eluding (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-395) at the time. 2nd degree requires only that a traffic violation directly caused the death. Multiple deaths from a single incident may result in multiple counts.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5 for 1st degree vehicular homicide. May be designated BDV requiring 90% of sentence before parole eligibility. 2nd degree (misdemeanor): parole does not apply.

title: Rape
description: A person commits rape when they have carnal knowledge of a female forcibly and against her will, or of a female who is less than 10 years of age. Carnal knowledge in rape occurs when there is any penetration of the female sex organ by the male sex organ.

options.label: Victim 10 years of age or older
options.sentence: Life or 25 years to Life (split sentence)
options.other: Mandatory 25-year minimum. Split sentence: minimum 25 years imprisonment followed by probation for life. Lifetime sex offender registration required.

options.label: Victim under 10 years of age
options.other: Lifetime sex offender registration required.

notes: Rape is a '7 Deadly Sin' offense. First Offender treatment is PROHIBITED. Death penalty appears in statute but has been held unconstitutional for rape (Coker v. Georgia, 1977; Kennedy v. Louisiana, 2008).
recidivist_info: Second conviction for rape or any serious violent felony mandates Life Without Parole under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-7(b)(2). Lifetime sex offender registration required under O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12.
parole_info: As a '7 Deadly Sin' offense, rape is generally not parole-eligible by statute except for life sentences (parole eligibility after 30 years). Conspiracy or attempt to commit rape is CSL 8; however, the associated percentage (65/75/90%) only applies to the CSL 8 portion of the sentence.

title: Sexual Battery
description: A person commits sexual battery when they intentionally make physical contact with the intimate parts of the body of another person without the consent of that person.

options.label: General (victim 16+, 1st offense)
options.other: Sex offender registration required

options.label: Victim under 16 years of age
options.other: Sex offender registration required

options.label: 2nd or subsequent offense (any victim)
options.other: Sex offender registration required

notes: 'Intimate parts' means the primary genital area, anus, groin, inner thighs, or buttocks of a male or female and the breasts of a female. Consent of a person under 16 is not a defense.
parole_info: CSL varies: CSL 1 for misdemeanor, CSL 3 for felony sexual battery. Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
description: It is unlawful for any person who has been convicted of a felony to receive, possess, or transport any firearm. Also applies to persons on first offender probation for a felony.
notes: Also applies to first offender probationers and persons convicted of certain forcible misdemeanors. 'Firearm' includes handguns, rifles, shotguns, and any weapon designed to propel a projectile by explosive or electrical charge. Certain exceptions exist for antique firearms. Civil rights restoration after 5 years (non-violent felonies) may restore firearm rights.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Carrying Weapon in Unauthorized Location
description: Carrying a weapon or long gun in an unauthorized location such as a government building, courthouse, jail or prison, place of worship without permission, state mental health facility, nuclear power facility, or within a school safety zone. Georgia enacted constitutional carry (SB 319) effective April 12, 2022, eliminating the weapons carry license requirement for lawful gun owners, but carry remains prohibited in certain locations.

options.label: Government building, courthouse, or place of worship

notes: Georgia's constitutional carry law (SB 319, effective April 12, 2022) eliminated the weapons carry license requirement for lawful adults. However, prohibited locations still apply regardless of license status. Prohibited persons (convicted felons, minors) cannot carry anywhere.
parole_info: CSL varies by location. School zone felony: CSL 3, requires 65% service. Misdemeanor: parole does not apply.

title: Use of Firearm During Commission of a Felony
description: Any person who uses a firearm while committing a felony is subject to an additional mandatory consecutive sentence. This sentence is served in addition to and consecutive with any other sentence imposed for the underlying felony.

options.label: 1st Offense
options.other: Mandatory 5-year consecutive sentence. Cannot be suspended, probated, stayed, deferred, or withheld.

options.label: 2nd Offense
options.other: Mandatory 10-year consecutive sentence. Cannot be suspended, probated, stayed, deferred, or withheld.

options.label: 3rd or Subsequent Offense
options.other: Mandatory 15-year consecutive sentence. Cannot be suspended, probated, stayed, deferred, or withheld.

notes: This sentence is CONSECUTIVE to the underlying felony sentence, not concurrent. The firearm enhancement cannot be merged with other charges. This is a separate charge that must be indicted and proven beyond a reasonable doubt. 'Use' includes having the firearm on one's person during the commission of the felony.
parole_info: The mandatory consecutive sentence must be served in full with no possibility of parole. This is served after the sentence for the underlying felony (though the underlying felony sentence may be parolable based on its own CSL).

title: Robbery
description: A person commits robbery when, with intent to commit theft, they take property of another from the person or the immediate presence of another by use of force, intimidation, threat, coercion, or by placing such person in fear of immediate serious bodily injury, or by sudden snatching.
notes: Robbery by sudden snatching carries a lesser penalty of 1-10 years. If a weapon is used, the charge is elevated to Armed Robbery under O.C.G.A. § 16-8-41 with a mandatory 10-year minimum. Robbery is NOT a '7 Deadly Sin' offense (armed robbery is).
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5 for robbery by force/intimidation. CSL 4 for robbery by sudden snatching. Robbery by force is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of sentence before parole eligibility.

title: Entering Automobile
description: A person commits the offense of entering an automobile when they enter any automobile or other motor vehicle with the intent to commit a theft or felony therein.
notes: Intent to commit theft or felony at the time of entry must be proven. Merely entering an unlocked vehicle without criminal intent is insufficient. This offense is frequently charged alongside theft by taking or criminal damage to property. Does not require forced entry - entering an unlocked vehicle with criminal intent is sufficient.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Criminal Damage to Property in the First Degree
description: A person commits criminal damage to property in the first degree when they knowingly and without authority interfere with any property in a manner so as to endanger human life, or knowingly and without authority damage the property of another person in excess of $500.
notes: Damage exceeding $500 or damage that endangers human life elevates to first degree (felony). Damage to utility property, traffic control devices, or fire safety equipment is automatically first degree regardless of value.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Criminal Damage to Property in the Second Degree
description: A person commits criminal damage to property in the second degree when they intentionally damage any property of another person without consent and the value of the damage is $500 or less.
notes: Damage of $500 or less. If the damage exceeds $500 or endangers human life, the offense is elevated to Criminal Damage in the First Degree (felony).
parole_info: Misdemeanor offense - parole does not apply.

title: Criminal Trespass
description: A person commits criminal trespass when they knowingly and without authority enter upon the land or premises of another person for an unlawful purpose, after receiving notice from the owner that such entry is forbidden, or remain upon the land or premises after being ordered to depart.
notes: Criminal trespass also includes intentionally damaging property of another ($500 or less) and knowingly and maliciously interfering with the possession or use of property without consent. Notice to depart may be verbal or by posted signs.
parole_info: Misdemeanor offense - parole does not apply.

title: Theft by Deception
description: A person commits theft by deception when they obtain property by any deceitful means or artful practice with the intention of depriving the owner of the property.
notes: Theft by deception includes creating or confirming false impressions of fact, failing to correct false impressions, preventing someone from acquiring relevant information, and selling or encumbering property while failing to disclose a known lien or adverse claim. Same value thresholds as Theft by Taking under O.C.G.A. § 16-8-12.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) varies by value: CSL 1 (misdemeanor, under $1,500), CSL 2 ($1,500-$5,000), CSL 3 ($5,000-$25,000), CSL 4 ($25,000+). Felony requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Arson in the First Degree
description: A person commits arson in the first degree when, by means of fire or explosive, they knowingly damage or cause another to damage any dwelling house of another without consent, or any structure or property in which a person is present.
notes: First degree arson applies to dwelling houses and occupied structures. If death results from arson, the charge may be elevated to felony murder under O.C.G.A. § 16-5-1(c). Arson to defraud an insurer is separately punishable.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5. Arson in the First Degree is a Board-Designated Violent (BDV) offense requiring 90% of the sentence to be served before parole eligibility.

title: Arson in the Second Degree
description: A person commits arson in the second degree when, by means of fire or explosive, they knowingly damage or cause another to damage any building, vehicle, or other property of another without consent, or any property owned by themselves with intent to defraud.
notes: Second degree arson applies to non-dwelling structures and unoccupied property. Includes burning one's own property to defraud an insurance company under O.C.G.A. § 16-7-61.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 3. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.

title: Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) - Schedule I/II
description: Possession of a Schedule I or II controlled substance with intent to distribute, sell, deliver, or manufacture. Intent to distribute may be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other circumstantial evidence. Commonly charged for amounts between simple possession and trafficking thresholds.
notes: PWID is charged when drug quantity exceeds personal use but falls below trafficking thresholds. Common indicators of intent: individually packaged drugs, scales, large cash amounts, multiple cell phones. Sentences significantly exceed simple possession (2-15 years vs. 5-30 years for 1st offense). Applies to cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, fentanyl, MDMA, and other Schedule I/II drugs.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 5-6 depending on substance and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. May be designated BDV depending on circumstances.

title: Possession with Intent to Distribute (PWID) - Schedule III/IV/V
description: Possession of a Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substance with intent to distribute, sell, deliver, or manufacture. Common Schedule III-V drugs include steroids, ketamine (III), Xanax, Valium (IV), and codeine cough syrup (V).
notes: Significantly lesser penalties than PWID Schedule I/II. Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol) carries enhanced penalties similar to Schedule I/II. PWID is charged based on quantity, packaging, and other circumstantial evidence of distribution intent.
parole_info: Crime Severity Level (CSL) 2-3 depending on substance and amount. Requires serving 65% of sentence before parole eligibility. Not a BDV offense.
